concern.concern: Step 1.1 says, 'Give X its natural finite CW structure with one vertex, core edges a,b,c, and 2-cells λ₂,λ₃'. Here X was defined as the union of two mapping cylinders: the common source circle c and the two target core circles are disjoint, so that actual space cannot have the asserted one-vertex structure with all three as core edges. The usual construction first includes the two connecting cylinder edges and then collapses their maximal tree to obtain the asserted presentation complex. That finite simple comparison is omitted from the claimed spine certificate.

cases.reason: The union of the two mapping cylinders has three distinct circle vertices and two connecting interval edges. It cannot itself have the asserted one-vertex core-cell structure. The missing maximal-tree quotient matters because this paragraph supplies a based simple-spine certificate, stronger than merely a group presentation. A finite tree contraction before the existing 2-cell slide preserves the full example and its torsion calculation.
cases.actual_supplier_and_use: F7 supplies the exterior boundary mapping-cylinder model with spine X; F2 requires a certified simple spine for torsion. The existing prism collapses concern exterior-to-X only; they do not identify the three vertices inside X. The proposed tree contraction completes that separate comparison.

replacements.source_excerpt: Choose finite cell structures compatible with this map and the two degree maps, and take the unique vertex of $X$ as basepoint. In the resulting mapping-cylinder CW structure, each prism over a boundary-torus cell $\sigma$ pairs with its unglued face $\sigma\times\{0\}$; removing these pairs in decreasing cell dimension gives a finite sequence of elementary collapses onto $X$, fixing $X$ and its chosen basepoint. Thus this specific exterior-to-$X$ equivalence is simple. Give $X$ its natural finite CW structure with one vertex, core edges $a,b,c$, and $2$-cells $\lambda_2,\lambda_3$ attached by $r_2=a^2c^{-1}$ and $r_3=b^3c^{-1}$.
replacements.proposed_replacement: Choose finite cell structures compatible with this map and the two degree maps, with circle vertices $v_c,v_a,v_b$ and cylinder edges $e_a:v_c\to v_a$, $e_b:v_c\to v_b$; take $v_c$ as basepoint. In the resulting exterior mapping-cylinder CW structure, each prism over a boundary-torus cell $\sigma$ pairs with its unglued face $\sigma\times\{0\}$; removing these pairs in decreasing cell dimension gives a finite sequence of elementary collapses onto $X$, fixing $X$ and $v_c$. Thus this specific exterior-to-$X$ equivalence is simple. The natural CW structure on $X$ has these three vertices, edges $a,b,c,e_a,e_b$, and $2$-cells with based words $e_a a^2e_a^{-1}c^{-1}$ and $e_b b^3e_b^{-1}c^{-1}$. The two connecting edges form a maximal tree. Contract it to obtain a based presentation complex $\overline X$: this contraction is simple, as can be seen by moving the loops and attaching paths at each terminal vertex across its connecting edge by cellular edge slides, then collapsing that edge with the now free terminal vertex. Each cellular slide is realized by an elementary expansion followed by an elementary collapse; the root $v_c$ is fixed. After the two contractions, $\overline X$ has one vertex, edges $a,b,c$, and $2$-cells $\lambda_2,\lambda_3$ attached by $r_2=a^2c^{-1}$ and $r_3=b^3c^{-1}$. Work in $\overline X$ for the following further simple changes.

concern.concern: Proof 2.1 applies the planar disk-slide supplier and says, “Two faces of a repeated other disk are processed separately.” The cited lem-marked-planar-cut-surface-regions-are-realized-by-disk-slides explicitly requires its inner faces to come from distinct disks. The proof should explain the successive one-face planar regions that permit repeated disk labels, rather than apply that supplier directly to the whole cap.

cases.reason: The named planar supplier requires all inner faces to have distinct disk labels, whereas the cap may contain both faces of one retained disk. Merely saying processed separately does not exhibit legal successive applications. The missing induction uses the supplier only with r=1, where the moving disk and each retained disk have distinct labels. It leaves the general closed-manifold and full-module claims intact.
cases.actual_supplier_and_use: lem-marked-planar-cut-surface-regions-are-realized-by-disk-slides Statement distinctness and Proof 3.1/4.1 implement a band sum and a cut-ball finger retraction fixing retained disks/arcs. A finite tree in the cap orders the face additions; each r=1 region surrounds just the current moving face and the next unused retained face, rather than the entire multiply labelled cap.

replacements.source_excerpt: [F6]'s planar construction slides $D_i$ across those faces until its outer rim is precisely $\partial D_i'$, followed by the empty-annulus isotopy. Two faces of a repeated other disk are processed separately.
replacements.proposed_replacement: Apply [F6]'s planar supplier successively with exactly two inner faces, rather than once to this whole cap. Choose a finite tree of disjoint joining bands in the cap, rooted at its unique $D_i$ face, and process it outward from the root. At each stage the frontier of a small neighborhood of the processed subtree is the moving rim. A thin neighborhood of that moving face, the next unused face and their joining band is a disk with two holes whose interior misses every other current face and z. Its two labels are the current moving disk and a retained $D_j$ with $j\ne i$, so the supplier's distinct-disk hypothesis holds with $r=1$. Its completed slide preserves the cut ball and the retained disks. Use its finger-retraction identification, supported at that face and band, to carry the unprocessed cap and its remaining faces to the new cut-ball boundary; outside that neighborhood the unused faces are unchanged. Thus the next stage has the same description. If both faces of a retained disk occur, the second remains an unused face of that retained disk and is processed by a later two-face application; it is never paired with its other face in one application. A tiny auxiliary trivial arc near z, with second endpoint w, can be fixed before this construction and missed by all these cap neighborhoods, so the supplier's marked arc condition is retained. After finitely many stages the moving rim is the frontier of the whole tree neighborhood, and the remaining empty annulus in the cap gives the isotopy to $\partial D_i'$.

replacements.proposed_replacement: 2.1 Regard $T$ and $T_0$ as finite linear complexes on the same embedded polyhedron $Q$. Form all nonempty cells $\sigma\cap\tau$ for $\sigma\in T$ and $\tau\in T_0$, together with their faces. By [F2] these form a finite convex cell complex covering $Q$, and a compatible finite simplicial triangulation $T'$ of that cell complex exists. Each simplex of $T'$ lies in a cell contained in a simplex of $T$ and a simplex of $T_0$, so $T'$ is a common linear refinement. In particular it is a subdivision of $T$. Every simplex of the subcomplex representing $f(P)$ is a union of these refined simplices; thus the simplices of $T'$ contained in $f(P)$ have realization exactly $f(P)$ and form a subcomplex by [F3]. [given, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct] ∎
